column1: # gate-commands.tsv - the gate's command units: the checks that are not
# `go test` of one package (edition vet, golangci-lint, the web suites),
# declared once and run by `testrunner gate` on its workers through
# tools/testrunner/bootstrap.sh exec, in the source tree, under the run's
# test timeout. A command unit passes on exit 0 and fails otherwise, with its
# output tail in the summary. The commands are the repo's own: each row says
# where it was taken from, and a change there must be mirrored here.
# Columns (tab separated; '#' lines and blank lines are ignored):
#   name      the unit's id and ledger key. {set} and {shard} are filled in
#             by the expansion.
#   expand    -            one unit
#             omit-sets    one unit per tag set `scripts/omit-tag-check.sh
#                          --list-tests --scope distro` prints (the editions and
#                          no_obs, what ci.yml runs per push; `testrunner
#                          gate --omit-scope all` lists every set, the
#                          dispatched matrix); {set} in the command is the
#                          set, {set} in
#                          the name its key (a distro set's sbo_distro_*
#                          stamp, else the set), and the weight is the set's
#                          row in omit-tag-weights.tsv (else this row's)
#             packages:N   N units over every package of the main module
#                          (go list ./... as GOOS=linux), dealt by weight
#                          (go-test-weights.tsv) longest first; {packages}
#                          in the command is the shard's ./dir list, {shard}
#                          in the name is i/N, and each gets weight/N
#   when      on an affected gate the row runs when a changed file matches
#             one entry: *.ext (suffix), dir/ (prefix) or an exact path;
#             always on --full
#   tools     - or a comma list: a tool pinned in gate-tools.tsv and
#             allowed by units.GateTools (node, golangci-lint, the SDK
#             runtimes nodeNN and python3.N, shellcheck, jdk17, maven),
#             own-tree (a fresh copy of the source for
#             a command that writes into the tree, so it never races the
#             other units of a multi-slot box; list it before git-index),
#             git-index (a git repository of the tree the command runs in,
#             for commands that call git)
#   weight_s  estimated seconds on a CI-sized runner (LPT order and the
#             spend projection only)
#   command   run by bash -c in the source tree
# vet: ci.yml's omit-tags job runs scripts/omit-tag-check.sh per set: go vet
#   -tags <set> ./..., plus the tagged packages' tests for the four editions.
#   The gate splits that in two so one edition is not one 20-minute unit:
#   this row runs the vet (--vet-only), and every package the editions test
#   (--list-tests) becomes a Go unit of its own run with -tags <set>
#   (<import>[<set key>], split like any Go unit at a quarter of its
#   split-table parts), triggered with this row. The script reads the tree
#   with git grep.
# lint: ci.yml's lint job (golangci-lint-action, version v2.14.0, default
#   args: golangci-lint run over ./...). Sharding by package keeps the
#   findings identical to the whole-tree run: every enabled linter analyses
#   one package at a time (facts from dependencies are computed either way),
#   the exclusions are path rules, and .golangci.yml sets no per-run issue
#   limits (max-issues-per-linter and max-same-issues are 0). The shards
#   together list exactly the packages ./... matches.
# web: ci.yml's frontend job (web) and ci-private.yml's frontend-web2 job
#   (web2), step by step, including their embedded-dist drift checks;
#   webcloud: the webcloud step of ci.yml's taxonomy-build-drift job (npm ci,
#   then make verify-webcloud-dist, which runs this script). shared/ has no
#   suite of its own; the three apps import it, so a shared/ change runs all
#   three.
vet:{set}
lint:{shard}
web:web
column6: cd web && npm ci && npm run typecheck && npm test && cd .. && node scripts/uicopylint/uicopylint.mjs web/src && cd web && npm run build && cd .. && scripts/sync-web-embed.sh web/dist internal/intelligence/dashboard/webapp/dist && { drift=$(git status --porcelain -- internal/intelligence/dashboard/webapp/dist); [ -z "$drift" ] || { echo "Committed webapp/dist drifted from web/dist. Run make web-build and commit the result."; echo "$drift" | head -40; exit 1; }; }

column1: web:web2
column6: cd web2 && npm ci && npm run typecheck && npm test && cd .. && node scripts/uicopylint/uicopylint.mjs web2/src && cd web2 && npm run build && cd .. && scripts/sync-web-embed.sh web2/dist internal/orgserver/dashboard/webapp/dist && { drift=$(git status --porcelain -- internal/orgserver/dashboard/webapp/dist); [ -z "$drift" ] || { echo "Committed orgserver webapp/dist drifted from web2/dist. Run make web-build-org and commit the result."; echo "$drift" | head -40; exit 1; }; }

column1: web:webcloud
column6: cd webcloud && npm ci && cd .. && scripts/verify-webcloud-dist.sh

column1: # migcheck: internal/migcheck's online migration rules (plan 06 18.2.4) over
#   the org PostgreSQL and cloud lineages; the pre-push hook runs it advisory.
#   Advisory here too until R1: it flips to --enforce at R1, when the M0.8
#   rules land in CLAUDE.md and M3a ships the non-transactional step class
migcheck
# orgstateinv: the org server's process-wide state against tools/orgstateinv/allowlist.tsv
#   (plan 07 M2.1). Its test reads the tree from disk, so cipkgs does not select it
#   on an org-server change; this row does.
orgstateinv
# structcheck: the managed-SaaS structural rules (plan 07 M3-0.8; tools/structcheck/doc.go
#   lists them): tenancy classes, new-table org_id, raw advisory locks, package state,
#   root files, imports_test pins and lease_gen are enforced; RLS policies, ON CONFLICT
#   targets and plan-name literals are advisory until M3b.1, M3a.4 and internal/entitlements.
#   S9 reads every package directory under internal/, hence the broad when.
structcheck
# opsgate: the Track E gate driver, the nightly and the train (plan 07 M11.2a, M11.2b, M11.3, M11.4; deploy/saas-ovh/ops,
#   deploy/saas-ovh/roll.sh). test-ops.sh runs nightly.sh against a throwaway git history with a built gatedriver, a
#   stubbed systemctl and a fake bisect runner (a seeded failure is named), and bash -n (shellcheck when installed) on
#   every ops script; test-roll.sh runs roll.sh's dry run and its promote, halt and inconclusive paths with stubbed
#   ssh, curl and judge. The Go rules are the tools/gatedriver and internal/trainhalt Go units.
opsgate
# gate-record: the L-145 gate record script (scripts/ci/gate-record.sh: build, check, add-images, show),
#   tested hermetically by test-gate-record.sh against a throwaway bare origin with stub runner and verifier
#   scripts (no Go, no network). It needs git, jq and tar; a missing jq fails the unit here instead of
#   the script's own SKIP, so a worker without jq never passes it silently.
gate-record
column6: command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "gate-record: jq is not installed"; exit 1; }; bash scripts/ci/test-gate-record.sh

column1: # drift: ci-private.yml's generated-file drift jobs that need only go, git and make
#   (L-139: the v1.39.0 release found stale OpenAPI stubs and a stale track sitemap
#   that no gate row had checked). The website accuracy check and
#   verify-distribution-readmes are units of their own (website-accuracy, drift:readmes,
#   below). Not here: verify-track-build: its sitemap <lastmod> dates come from
#   `git log`, and the git-index snapshot is one commit made today, so every page would
#   read as changed; it is the host check host:track-build
#   (scripts/ci/gate-host-checks.tsv), run in a checkout with the real history. verify-docs-build masks the
#   two git-derived page dates for the same reason, so it runs here; docs/sdk/ and
#   shared/lib/productNames.json are in `when` because gen publishes the first
#   (nav.toml [roots] sdk) and expands @@name@@ tokens from the second. git-index: the
#   scripts start with git rev-parse --show-toplevel.
drift
column6: make verify-openapi verify-website-build verify-docs-build verify-w8-claims verify-adapter-parity-doc verify-guard-coverage-ts

column1: # drift:docs-index: the dated doc index step of ci-private.yml's adapter-parity-doc
#   job (make verify-docs-index: docs/{plans,audits,handovers}/INDEX.md against a
#   fresh render of tools/docsindexgen). Its own unit, not part of drift, so a
#   change that touches only a dated doc runs this check alone. git-index: the
#   generator lists the folders with git ls-files.
drift:docs-index
# website-tests: ci-private.yml's website worker tests.
website-tests
# aggregate-collector: the hosted aggregate collector's Worker tests
#   (deploy/aggregate-collector/README.md "Test it", its package.json test script):
#   node:test over a node:sqlite D1 stand-in with the migrations applied. The tests
#   import only Node built-ins and committed files, so no npm ci. node: the pinned
#   Node 22 (node:sqlite needs 22.13+). No GitHub workflow runs them: the collector
#   is deployed by hand, never from CI. A schema change regenerates
#   deploy/aggregate-collector/schema/, so the path covers tools/aggregateschemagen too.
aggregate-collector
# sdk: the SDK matrix (plan W2-4 and principle 9, lane B4): sdk/python on
#   every CPython its requires-python admits (3.9 to 3.13) and sdk/typescript
#   on Node 20, 22 and 24 (Node 18 dropped: past end of life), each on the runtime pinned in gate-tools.tsv;
#   sdk:pack builds the release artifacts exactly as npm-release.yml's
#   sdk_pack job does (scripts/ci/sdk.sh pack); sdk:e2e is the contract suite against a real
#   machine and a real org gateway (tests/sdke2e: builds observer and
#   observer-org, starts both on scratch ports with a private PostgreSQL,
#   runs both SDKs' example apps to the local, online and both destinations
#   and checks the spans landed with identity, tokens and cost). sdk.sh
#   copies the package into the unit's TMPDIR, so the units share the tree
#   safely. sdk:e2e needs PostgreSQL 16 binaries on the worker (initdb,
#   pg_ctl; on PATH or under /usr/lib/postgresql/*/bin), or a server named
#   by OBSERVER_CONTROL_STORE_DSN.
#   sdk:java-17 is ci.yml's sdk job's java-17 leg (setup-java temurin 17 and
#   the runner's Maven): sdk.sh java (mvn test) on the Temurin 17 JDK and the
#   Maven pinned in gate-tools.tsv, with JAVA_HOME set to that JDK as
#   setup-java sets it. Maven fetches its plugins and the test dependencies
#   from Maven Central (repo.maven.apache.org) into the unit user's ~/.m2.
sdk:python-3.9
sdk:python-3.10
sdk:python-3.11
sdk:python-3.12
sdk:python-3.13
sdk:node-20
sdk:node-22
sdk:node-24
sdk:java-17
column6: JAVA_HOME="$(dirname "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$(command -v java)")")")" && export JAVA_HOME && bash scripts/ci/sdk.sh java

column1: # sdk:widget-*: the end-user feedback widget (@superbased/feedback-widget),
#   which releases with the SDKs on their version line (review E-11): its
#   typecheck and tests on every Node major the SDK is tested on.
sdk:widget-node-20
sdk:widget-node-22
sdk:widget-node-24
# sdk:install-strings: every "not published yet" install string is in one
#   state, so the release-day flip (scripts/sdk-install-strings.py flip,
#   review E-66) rewrites them all.
# sdk:go: sdk/go (Go module github.com/superbasedapp/observer/sdk/go, lane
#   SDK-go): gofmt, go vet and go test -race against sdk/contract, on the go
#   toolchain the gate already runs (no new tool).
sdk:go
sdk:install-strings
sdk:pack
sdk:e2e
# planea-e2e:unit: the AI Apps live e2e runner's unit tests (review P-36): the
#   runner's pure parts and its safety checks (no provider contacted in a dry
#   run, the allow-listed child environment, DSN redaction, the host guard, the
#   spend cap), and the setup run's (setup_run.py, the SDK quickstart's live
#   check), no network, no daemon. planea-e2e:dry (the full dry run,
#   scripts/planea-e2e/run.sh --dry-run --destination all) joins when the gate's
#   workers have PostgreSQL 16 for the throwaway org.
planea-e2e:unit
column6: python3 -m unittest scripts/planea-e2e/test_e2e.py && python3 -m unittest scripts/planea-e2e/test_setup_run.py

column1: # Jobs the gate stands in for so that GitHub runs only what needs GitHub
# (docs/plans/ci-github-only-what-needs-github-2026-11-21.md, section 9.1;
# the shard reports these units land in are combined into one unsigned gate
# record by scripts/ci/gate-record.sh). Each row runs its job's steps minus
# the GitHub-only setup (checkout, setup-*, caches, the free-disk step); a
# job that wrote bin/ writes under the unit's $TMPDIR instead, removed on
# exit.
# govet:linux, govet:windows, copylint, build:observer, build:windows:
#   ci.yml's go job, one unit per step: vet, vet (windows), copy lint, build
#   (the observer and the Windows antigravity-bridge, into $TMPDIR, not
#   bin/), windows cross-compile (go build of several packages writes
#   nothing). The job's latency step is the host check host:latency
#   (scripts/ci/gate-host-checks.tsv: it needs an idle box) and its
#   toolchain tests run in the gate's tests/invariant unit (the runner does
#   not set SBO_SKIP_TOOLCHAIN_TESTS). copylint reads Go, docs, website copy
#   and the workflows, hence its when.
govet:linux
govet:windows
copylint
build:observer
column6: o="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/build.XXXXXX")" && trap 'rm -rf "$o"' EXIT && go build -trimpath -o "$o/observer" ./cmd/observer && GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build -trimpath -o "$o/antigravity-bridge.exe" ./cmd/antigravity-bridge && ls -l "$o"

column1: build:windows
# distro:*: ci.yml's distros job, one unit per matrix leg: build + proof +
#   SBOM (scripts/build-distro.sh <d> --proof, with --out under $TMPDIR in
#   place of bin/distro; distro-smoke.sh refuses a binary under /tmp, and a
#   worker's TMPDIR is /var/tmp/sXXXX, hence the /var/tmp default), then
#   the listener smoke (scripts/distro-smoke.sh, in its own user, mount and
#   network namespace: the box needs unprivileged user namespaces, which
#   WSL and the cloud boxes have; the job's apparmor sysctl is the GitHub
#   runner's). The full leg skips on a tree without cmd/observer/obs_wire.go
#   (the public snapshot), as the job does.
distro:minimal
column6: o="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/var/tmp}/distro.XXXXXX")" && trap 'rm -rf "$o"' EXIT && scripts/build-distro.sh minimal --proof --out "$o" && scripts/distro-smoke.sh "$o/observer-minimal-$(go env GOOS)-$(go env GOARCH)"

column1: distro:developer
column6: o="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/var/tmp}/distro.XXXXXX")" && trap 'rm -rf "$o"' EXIT && scripts/build-distro.sh developer --proof --out "$o" && scripts/distro-smoke.sh "$o/observer-developer-$(go env GOOS)-$(go env GOARCH)"

column1: distro:managed
column6: o="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/var/tmp}/distro.XXXXXX")" && trap 'rm -rf "$o"' EXIT && scripts/build-distro.sh managed --proof --out "$o" && scripts/distro-smoke.sh "$o/observer-managed-$(go env GOOS)-$(go env GOARCH)"

column1: distro:full
column6: if [ ! -f cmd/observer/obs_wire.go ]; then echo "distro full skipped, this tree has no cmd/observer/obs_wire.go (the public snapshot)"; exit 0; fi; o="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/var/tmp}/distro.XXXXXX")" && trap 'rm -rf "$o"' EXIT && scripts/build-distro.sh full --proof --out "$o" && scripts/distro-smoke.sh "$o/observer-full-$(go env GOOS)-$(go env GOARCH)"

column1: # installer:linux: ci.yml's installer job, Linux leg (the macOS and Windows
#   legs stay on GitHub): shellcheck (pinned, gate-tools.tsv), the
#   mxc-files.sh offline checks, then scripts/test-install.sh against a
#   fixture release signed by a vendorsign built into $TMPDIR (the job's
#   $RUNNER_TEMP). node is on PATH, as on the GitHub runner, so the test's
#   node Ed25519 verifier case runs too. test-install.sh hands the caller's
#   PATH to install.sh, which refuses a second copy when an `observer` is
#   already on PATH (a WSL box sees the Windows PATH, often with an npm
#   install of observer; the GitHub runner has none), so the test runs with
#   every PATH directory holding an observer left out.
installer:linux
column6: shellcheck scripts/install.sh scripts/test-install.sh && bash scripts/test-mxc-files.sh && vs="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/vendorsign.XXXXXX")" && trap 'rm -rf "$vs"' EXIT && go build -o "$vs/vendorsign" ./scripts/vendorsign && clean_path="$(printf '%s' "$PATH" | tr : '\n' | while IFS= read -r d; do if [ -n "$d" ] && [ ! -e "$d/observer" ]; then printf '%s:' "$d"; fi; done)" && PATH="${clean_path%:}" VENDORSIGN_BIN="$vs/vendorsign" bash scripts/test-install.sh

column1: # drift:plugins: ci.yml's plugins-build-drift job (web's npm ci, then make
#   verify-plugins-build, then the plugins-repo assembly self-check).
#   plugingen runs the real observer init registrars (about 150 packages
#   of this module), so any Go change triggers it. own-tree: npm ci writes
#   node_modules into the tree.
drift:plugins
column6: cd web && npm ci && cd .. && make verify-plugins-build && bash scripts/assemble-plugins-repo.sh --self-check

column1: # drift:taxonomy: ci.yml's taxonomy-build-drift job (web's npm ci, then its
#   seven make verify-* steps in order, one make stopping at the first
#   failure as the job stops at its first failed step); its webcloud step is
#   the web:webcloud unit. The generators read Go source (cfgschema parses
#   internal/config's doc comments; about 35 packages in all), shared/lib,
#   web/src/lib, the migrations and testdata/agentconfig, hence its when.
#   own-tree: npm ci.
drift:taxonomy
column6: cd web && npm ci && cd .. && make verify-taxonomy-build verify-taxonomy-ts verify-taxonomy-migration verify-assistant-migration verify-reasoning-migration verify-config-schema verify-agentconfig-catalog

column1: # drift:readmes: ci-private.yml's distribution-readmes job (make
#   verify-distribution-readmes: the npm and PyPI READMEs against their
#   templates and the shared body), with the pinned Python 3.12's python3.
#   git-index: the script starts with git rev-parse --show-toplevel.
drift:readmes
# website-accuracy: ci-private.yml's website-accuracy job, whose two steps
#   live in scripts/ci/website-accuracy.sh (the job and release.sh preflight
#   call it too). It asks the public GitHub API (api.github.com, no token
#   here) whether the canonical release is published and, where the API
#   cannot answer (a cloud worker's allowlist proxy answers it 403), the
#   public repository's tags over git ls-remote on github.com, then runs
#   website/tools/accuracy-check.mjs over the site and its canonical sources.
website-accuracy
# model-pricing-pg: ci-private.yml's model-pricing-pg job (the model-pricing
#   module's ./internal/observerexport/... against a live PostgreSQL,
#   failing on a PRICING_DSN skip), in scripts/ci/model-pricing-pg.sh with a
#   private PostgreSQL from the worker's binaries (initdb and pg_ctl, 16 or
#   newer, like sdk:e2e) in place of the job's postgres:16 service.
model-pricing-pg
# image:full, image:core: ci-private.yml's org-image-proof job, one unit per
#   matrix leg (scripts/build-distro.sh --image <i> --proof: build, proof,
#   SBOM), with --out under $TMPDIR in place of bin/distro.
image:full
image:core
